subQuestions.questionText:
Match each term in Column A with the correct definition in Column B. Write only the question number and the matching letter (e.g. 1.1.1 D).

Column A:
1.1.1 Perimeter
1.1.2 Volume
1.1.3 Probability
1.1.4 Ratio
1.1.5 Median

Column B:
A. The middle value when data is sorted from smallest to largest.
B. The amount of space inside a 3-D object, measured in cubic units.
C. A comparison of two quantities, written in the form a : b.
D. The total distance around the outside edge of a 2-D shape.
E. The chance of an event happening, given as a fraction, decimal or percentage.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: 1.1.1 D ✓ (Perimeter — total distance around the outside edge of a 2-D shape)
Mark 2: 1.1.2 B ✓ (Volume — amount of space inside a 3-D object)
Mark 3: 1.1.3 E ✓ (Probability — chance of an event happening)
Mark 4: 1.1.4 C ✓ (Ratio — a comparison written a : b)
Mark 5: 1.1.5 A ✓ (Median — middle value of sorted data)
[Award 1 mark per correct match]

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the average maximum temperature of Durban in December.
(Refer to the Summer Holiday Infographic table in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $28°C$ ✓
[Award 1 mark for correctly reading the value from the table]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the RANGE of the average maximum temperatures across the five cities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify highest = $30°C$ (Bloemfontein) and lowest = $25°C$ (Port Elizabeth) ✓
Mark 2: Range = $30 - 25 = 5°C$ ✓
[Award 1 mark for identifying max/min, 1 mark for correct answer with units]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the MEAN average rainfall across the five cities. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Sum = $15 + 108 + 125 + 85 + 47 = 380$ mm ✓
Mark 2: Mean = $380 \div 5$ ✓
Mark 3: Mean = $76,00$ mm ✓
[Award method marks even if final answer incorrect]

subQuestions.questionText: The Naidoo family wants a HOT and DRY beach holiday in December. Use the table to recommend ONE city. Justify your answer using TWO values from the table.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify HOT = highest max temperature ✓
Mark 2: Identify DRY = lowest rainfall ✓
Mark 3: Quote two correct values from the table ✓
Mark 4: Make a recommendation with justification ✓

Recommended: BLOEMFONTEIN — it is the HOTTEST ($30°C$) and reasonably dry ($85$ mm), making it the best choice for a HOT and DRY beach holiday.

[Also award full marks if candidate justifies Port Elizabeth using DRY as the priority and lists $47$ mm + $25°C$ clearly. The explanation mark is only awarded if a full sentence with data values is written.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the missing values A, B, C and D in the Learner Transport Survey table.

(Refer to TABLE 1 in the question paper.)
ONE learner is chosen at random from the survey. Write the probability that the learner is a girl who takes a taxi as a fraction in simplest form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Girls who take a taxi = $B = 25$ ✓
Mark 2: $P = \dfrac{25}{200}$ ✓
Mark 3: Simplify by dividing both by 25: $P = \dfrac{1}{8}$ ✓

Final: $P(\text{girl who takes a taxi}) = \dfrac{1}{8}$

subQuestions.questionText: Express the number of learners who walk as a percentage of the total number of learners surveyed. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\% = \dfrac{70}{200} \times 100$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 35,00\%$ ✓
[Award method mark even if value of D is incorrect — consequential marking]

subQuestions.questionText: A teacher claims: "At our school, more boys walk than girls." State whether this claim is VALID and give ONE reason, using values from the table.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: ✓ The claim is NOT VALID. Only $30$ boys walk, while $40$ girls walk, so MORE girls walk than boys.
[Award the mark only when the candidate writes a sentence using both values (30 and 40). A simple yes/no without data does not earn the mark.]

questions.title: Map and Layout — School Sports Day

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the GENERAL DIRECTION (compass direction) when walking from the Main Gate (A) to the Athletics Track (C).
(Refer to DIAGRAM A: Layout Plan of School Sports Day in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Recognise A is in the south-west and C is towards the north ✓
Mark 2: State direction ✓

Answer: NORTH (or NORTH-EAST — accept either, since C is roughly north and slightly east of A).

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the TWO facilities that are directly south of the Food Stalls (F).
(Refer to DIAGRAM A in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Rugby Field (D) ✓
Mark 2: Soccer Field (E) ✓
[Award 1 mark per correct facility]

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Khumalo enters at the Main Gate (A) and wants to take the most direct walking path to the First Aid Tent (G). Describe his route in one or two short sentences, using compass directions and the labels on the map.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct general starting direction (e.g. north or north-east) ✓
Mark 2: Mention of at least one named facility along the route (e.g. Rugby Field D or Food Stalls F) ✓
Mark 3: Logical/coherent path described ✓
Mark 4: Named end at G (First Aid) ✓

Example: "From the Main Gate (A), walk NORTH-EAST past the Rugby Field (D), continue NORTH along the side of the Food Stalls (F), and the First Aid tent (G) is directly north of the food stalls."

subQuestions.questionText:
On the plan, the Athletics Track measures 6,5 cm long. Calculate the actual (real) length of the Athletics Track in metres.
(The plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 500.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Real distance = plan distance × scale factor = $6,5 \times 500$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 3\,250$ cm ✓
Mark 3: Convert to metres: $3\,250 \div 100 = 32,50$ m ✓

Final: Real length = $32,50$ m

subQuestions.questionText: On the plan, the straight-line distance between the Main Gate (A) and the Stage (H) measures 9,2 cm. Calculate the actual distance in metres.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{Real} = 9,2 \times 500$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 4\,600$ cm ✓
Mark 3: Convert: $4\,600 \div 100 = 46,00$ m ✓

Final: Real distance = $46,00$ m

subQuestions.questionText: Mrs Pillay says: "The Rugby Field is more than 20 m wide." On the plan, the Rugby Field measures 3,2 cm wide. Verify, with calculations, whether her statement is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Real width = $3,2 \times 500 = 1\,600$ cm ✓
Mark 2: Convert: $1\,600 \div 100 = 16$ m ✓
Mark 3: Compare: $16$ m vs $20$ m → $16 < 20$ ✓
Mark 4: Conclusion in a full sentence ✓

The claim is NOT VALID. The actual width of the rugby field is only $16$ m, which is LESS THAN $20$ m. So Mrs Pillay is incorrect.

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the probability of choosing a HOT FOOD stall. Give your answer as a percentage.
(The Food Stalls area contains 12 stalls: 4 hot food, 5 cold drinks, 3 crafts.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $P = \dfrac{4}{12}$ ✓
Mark 2: As percentage: $0,3333... \times 100 = 33,33\%$ ✓

Final: $P(\text{hot food stall}) = 33,33\%$

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability that the chosen stall is NOT a craft stall. Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Not craft = $12 - 3 = 9$ stalls ✓
Mark 2: $P = \dfrac{9}{12}$ ✓
Mark 3: Simplify by dividing by 3: $P = \dfrac{3}{4}$ ✓

Final: $P(\text{not craft}) = \dfrac{3}{4}$

subQuestions.questionText: 240 learners visit the Food Stalls during the day, each choosing a random stall. Predict how many of these learners will buy at a cold drinks stall. Show your working.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $P(\text{cold drinks}) = \dfrac{5}{12}$ ✓
Mark 2: Expected number = $\dfrac{5}{12} \times 240$ ✓
Mark 3: $= 5 \times 20 = 100$ learners ✓

Final: $100$ learners are expected to buy at a cold drinks stall.

subQuestions.questionText:
Two parents arrive late and want to watch the athletics events at the Track (C). Parent X parks at the formal Parking Lot (B) at the south-east corner. Parent Y parks informally next to the Rugby Field (D) and walks across the field. Both want to reach the Athletics Track quickly.

Using DIAGRAM A, advise the school which parent made the BETTER choice. Give TWO reasons that refer to the layout (e.g. distance, safety, the events on the rugby field).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: State which parent made the better choice ✓
Marks 2–3: Two valid reasons referencing the layout ✓✓
Mark 4: Explanation refers to the actual scenario / data ✓

Parent X (formal Parking Lot) made the BETTER choice. Reasons: (1) it is a designated parking area, so the car is safer; AND (2) walking on the rugby field while events are taking place is unsafe and disruptive. Even though Parent Y is closer in metres, the safety and disruption concerns outweigh the small distance saved.

[Accept other reasonable answers that use the layout, e.g. clear path vs crossing live event area.]

questions.title: Measurement — Community Garden and Water Tank

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the total area covered by the FOUR vegetable beds.
(Each bed measures 5 m × 1,5 m. Refer to DIAGRAM B in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Area of one bed = $5 \times 1,5$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 7,5$ m² ✓
Mark 3: Total = $4 \times 7,5 = 30$ m² ✓

Final: Total area = $30$ m²

subQuestions.questionText:
The full plot will be fenced. Calculate the total length of fencing needed (the perimeter of the plot).
(The plot measures 12 m by 8 m.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $P = 2 \times (12 + 8) = 2 \times 20$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 40$ m ✓

Final: Perimeter = $40$ m

subQuestions.questionText: Fencing wire costs R85,50 per metre (excluding VAT). Calculate the cost of the fencing wire EXCLUDING VAT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Cost = length × rate = $40 \times R85,50$ ✓
Mark 2: Correct multiplication ✓
Mark 3: $= R3\,420,00$ ✓

Final: Cost (excl. VAT) = $R3\,420,00$

subQuestions.questionText: Add 15% VAT to the answer in QUESTION 3.1.3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: VAT amount = $15\% \times 3\,420 = 0,15 \times 3\,420 = R513,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Cost incl. VAT = $3\,420 + 513 = R3\,933,00$ ✓

[Alternative: $3\,420 \times 1,15 = R3\,933,00$]

Final: Cost incl. VAT = $R3\,933,00$

subQuestions.questionText: The committee budgeted R3 800,00 for fencing. Verify whether the budget is enough to pay for the fencing INCLUDING VAT. Show all calculations and write a sentence with your conclusion.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Compare: $R3\,800,00$ (budget) vs $R3\,933,00$ (cost). $3\,800 < 3\,933$ → short by $R133,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Conclusion in a full sentence ✓

The budget is NOT enough. The fencing including VAT will cost $R3\,933,00$, which is $R133,00$ more than the $R3\,800,00$ budgeted. The committee will need to find an extra $R133,00$ or buy fewer metres of fencing.

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the radius (r) of the tank, in metres.
(The tank has diameter 1,4 m and height 1,8 m.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $r = \dfrac{d}{2} = \dfrac{1,4}{2} = 0,7$ m ✓

Final: $r = 0,7$ m

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the volume of water the tank can hold when full. Give your answer in m³, then convert to litres.
(Use $\pi = 3,142$ and $1$ m³ $= 1\,000$ L.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $V = \pi \times r^2 \times h$ (correct formula) ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $V = 3,142 \times (0,7)^2 \times 1,8$ ✓
Mark 3: $V = 3,142 \times 0,49 \times 1,8$ ✓
Mark 4: $V \approx 2,77$ m³ ✓
Mark 5: Convert: $2,77 \times 1\,000 = 2\,771,28$ L ✓

Final: Volume $\approx 2,77$ m³ $= 2\,771,28$ L

subQuestions.questionText:
The OUTSIDE curved surface (the side wall) of the tank must be painted. Calculate the curved surface area, in m². Round to TWO decimal places.
(Use the formula: Curved Surface Area = $2 \times \pi \times r \times h$.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $\text{CSA} = 2 \times \pi \times r \times h$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 2 \times 3,142 \times 0,7 \times 1,8$ ✓
Mark 3: $\approx 7,92$ m² ✓

Final: CSA $\approx 7,92$ m²

subQuestions.questionText: Paint costs R45,00 per litre, and 1 litre of paint covers 6 m². Calculate the cost of the paint needed for the curved surface. Round up to the nearest whole litre when buying paint.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Paint needed = $\dfrac{7,92}{6} = 1,32$ litres ✓
Mark 2: Round UP to nearest whole litre = $2$ L ✓
Mark 3: Cost = $2 \times R45,00 = R90,00$ ✓

Final: Cost of paint = $R90,00$

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate how many days a FULL tank can supply 80 litres per day.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Recall full tank = $2\,771,28$ L (from 3.2.2) ✓
Mark 2: Set up: Days = Volume ÷ Daily use = $\dfrac{2\,771,28}{80}$ ✓
Mark 3: Correct division ✓
Mark 4: $\approx 34,64$ days (or about $34$ full days) ✓

Final: $\approx 34$ days (or $34,64$ days)

subQuestions.questionText: Verify Mr Dlamini's claim that "When the tank is full, it can supply the garden with water for AT LEAST 30 days, if we use 80 litres per day." End with a full sentence stating whether the claim is VALID or NOT VALID, and why.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Calculated days $\approx 34$; Claim: at least $30$ ✓
Mark 2: Compare: $34 > 30$ ✓
Mark 3: Conclusion in a full sentence ✓

The claim is VALID. A full tank can supply about $34$ days of water at $80$ L per day, which is MORE than the $30$ days Mr Dlamini stated. The community will have about $4$ extra days of water.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO realistic ways the school could make the tank water last longer.
Explain in a short sentence why ONLY the curved surface is painted, and not the top and bottom of the tank.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identifies that top/bottom are not exposed to weather/sunlight ✓
Mark 2: Practical reason given (saves paint/money or only the side needs protection) ✓

Example: The TOP and BOTTOM of the tank are not normally exposed to direct sunlight or weather (the bottom rests on the ground or a stand, and the top has a sealed lid), so they do not need protective paint. Only the curved (side) surface is exposed to sun and rain, so painting only the curved surface saves paint and money.

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the family's TOTAL monthly bill under Option A. Show all blocks and the service charge separately.
(The Mokoena family uses 480 kWh per month. Option A — Postpaid Inclining Block Tariff: Block 1 (0–50 kWh) at R1,85; Block 2 (>50 to 350 kWh) at R2,55; Block 3 (>350 kWh) at R3,75; plus a fixed monthly service charge of R120,00.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Block 1: $50 \times R1,85 = R92,50$ ✓
Mark 2: Identify Block 2 kWh: $350 - 50 = 300$ kWh ✓
Mark 3: Block 2: $300 \times R2,55 = R765,00$ ✓
Mark 4: Identify Block 3 kWh: $480 - 350 = 130$ kWh; Block 3: $130 \times R3,75 = R487,50$ ✓
Mark 5: Service charge: $R120,00$ ✓
Mark 6: Total = $92,50 + 765,00 + 487,50 + 120,00 = R1\,465,00$ ✓

Final: Option A total = $R1\,465,00$

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the AVERAGE cost per kWh under Option A. Round to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Average = $\dfrac{R1\,465,00}{480}$ ✓
Mark 2: $= R3,05$ per kWh ✓

Final: Average = $R3,05$ per kWh

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the family's monthly bill under Option B.
(Option B — Prepaid flat rate: R2,95 per kWh, no service charge.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Cost = $480 \times R2,95$ ✓
Mark 2: $= R1\,416,00$ ✓

Final: Option B total = $R1\,416,00$

subQuestions.questionText: Determine which option is CHEAPER for 480 kWh and by how many rand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Difference = $R1\,465,00 - R1\,416,00 = R49,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Identify cheaper option in a sentence ✓

Option B (prepaid) is CHEAPER by $R49,00$ for $480$ kWh.

subQuestions.questionText: Mr Mokoena says: "Prepaid is always cheaper because there is no service charge." Comment on his statement, using your answers in QUESTION 4.1. Write at least one full sentence.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Acknowledge that prepaid IS cheaper at $480$ kWh (by $R49,00$) ✓
Mark 2: Identify that the claim of "always" is too strong ✓
Mark 3: Explanation referring to low usage where Block 1/2 rates are cheaper than $R2,95$ ✓

Example: Mr Mokoena's statement is PARTIALLY VALID. Prepaid IS slightly cheaper for THIS family at $480$ kWh (saving $R49,00$), but the claim that prepaid is ALWAYS cheaper is NOT correct. At low usage, postpaid Block 1 ($R1,85$) and Block 2 ($R2,55$) rates can make it cheaper overall, even with the service charge.

subQuestions.questionText: If the family REDUCED their usage to 200 kWh per month, calculate the new bill under EACH option and state which option becomes cheaper.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Option A — Block 1: $50 \times R1,85 = R92,50$ ✓
Mark 2: Option A — Block 2: $(200-50) = 150$ kWh × $R2,55 = R382,50$ ✓
Mark 3: Option A total: $92,50 + 382,50 + 120,00 = R595,00$ ✓
Mark 4: Option B: $200 \times R2,95 = R590,00$ ✓
Mark 5: Comparison and conclusion: Difference $= R5,00$; Option B still cheaper but only by $R5,00$ ✓

Final: At $200$ kWh, Option B is still slightly cheaper, but only by $R5,00$ (almost the same). At even lower usage, Option A would become cheaper.

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the missing values A (a percentage) and B (a number of households) in TABLE 2.
(Refer to TABLE 2 — Municipal Survey of 500 households in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $A\% = \dfrac{180}{500} \times 100$ ✓
Mark 2: $A = 36\%$ ✓
Mark 3: $B = 16\% \times 500 = 0,16 \times 500$ ✓
Mark 4: $B = 80$ households ✓

[Check: $36 + 48 + 16 = 100\%$ ✓]

Final: $A = 36\%$ and $B = 80$ households

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability that a randomly chosen household in the survey uses prepaid. Give your answer as a decimal.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $P = \dfrac{240}{500}$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 0,48$ ✓

Final: $P(\text{prepaid}) = 0,48$

subQuestions.questionText: Write the number of postpaid households to the number of solar households as a ratio in simplest form.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify Postpaid = $180$, Solar = $80$ ✓
Mark 2: Ratio = $180 : 80$ ✓
Mark 3: Simplify by dividing by HCF $20$: $9 : 4$ ✓

Final: Ratio = $9 : 4$

subQuestions.questionText: The municipality claims: "More than HALF of all households use prepaid OR solar." Verify the claim, showing all calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Prepaid + Solar = $240 + 80 = 320$ households ✓
Mark 2: Half of $500 = 250$ ✓
Mark 3: Compare: $320 > 250$ ✓
Mark 4: Conclusion (sentence with data) ✓

The claim is VALID. $320$ out of $500$ households ($64,00\%$) use prepaid OR solar, which is MORE than half ($50\%$ or $250$ households).

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ONE practical reason why so many households choose prepaid over postpaid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reasonable practical reason ✓
Mark 2: Written as a full sentence ✓

Accept any ONE reasonable answer, e.g.
• "Prepaid lets households control their spending and avoid bill shock."
• "There is no service charge or risk of disconnection for unpaid bills."
• "It is easier for low-income households to budget by buying small amounts of electricity at a time."
• "There is no monthly contract or paperwork."

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the time, in minutes, that each route would take. (Convert hours to minutes.)
(Route 1: Highway — 18 km at 90 km/h. Route 2: Town roads — 14 km at 50 km/h. Use Time = Distance ÷ Speed.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Route 1 — Time = $\dfrac{18}{90}$ ✓
Mark 2: $= 0,2$ hours ✓
Mark 3: $= 0,2 \times 60 = 12$ minutes ✓
Mark 4: Route 2 — Time = $\dfrac{14}{50} = 0,28$ hours ✓
Mark 5: $= 0,28 \times 60 = 16,80$ minutes ✓

Final: Route 1 $\approx 12$ minutes; Route 2 $\approx 16,80$ minutes ($\approx 16$ min $48$ s)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine which route is faster, and by how many minutes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify times: Route 1 = $12$ min, Route 2 = $16,80$ min ✓
Mark 2: Difference = $16,80 - 12 = 4,80$ minutes ✓
Mark 3: Identify Route 1 (highway) as faster ✓

Final: Route 1 (highway) is FASTER by $4,80$ minutes ($\approx 4$ min $48$ s).

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from time, give ONE practical reason why the planner might still choose the LONGER route. Write a full sentence.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Practical, valid reason ✓
Mark 2: Written as a full sentence ✓

Accept any ONE valid reason, e.g.
• "The town route avoids the highway, which may have heavy weekend traffic or roadworks."
• "The town route is safer at night because it has streetlights."
• "The town route passes by a refuelling station / restroom that the guests may need."
• "The town route may have lower speed limits, which is safer for guests."

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the MINIMUM number of large buses Company X must send so that all 124 guests are transported.
(Company X — large bus, capacity 25 guests, R3 200 per bus per one-way trip.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $124 \div 25 = 4,96$ ✓
Mark 2: Round UP — cannot send a fraction of a bus → $5$ buses ✓

Final: $5$ buses ($4$ buses carry only $100$ guests, so $5$ are needed).

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the MINIMUM number of minibuses Company Y must send so that all 124 guests are transported.
(Company Y — minibus, capacity 14 guests, R1 450 per minibus per one-way trip.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: $124 \div 14 = 8,857...$ ✓
Mark 2: Round UP → $9$ minibuses ✓

Final: $9$ minibuses ($8$ carry only $112$ guests, so $9$ are needed).

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the TOTAL one-way cost for EACH company, based on your answers in QUESTION 5.2.1 and 5.2.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Company X cost setup: $5 \times R3\,200$ ✓
Mark 2: Company X cost = $R16\,000,00$ ✓
Mark 3: Company Y cost setup: $9 \times R1\,450$ ✓
Mark 4: Company Y cost = $R13\,050,00$ ✓

Final: Company X = $R16\,000,00$; Company Y = $R13\,050,00$

subQuestions.questionText: The planner claims: "Choosing the cheaper company will save us more than R2 500." Verify this claim, using your costs from QUESTION 5.2.3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Saving = $R16\,000,00 - R13\,050,00 = R2\,950,00$ ✓
Mark 2: Compare: $R2\,950,00 > R2\,500,00$ ✓
Mark 3: Conclusion in a full sentence ✓

The claim is VALID. Choosing Company Y saves the wedding party $R2\,950,00$, which is $R450,00$ more than the $R2\,500,00$ the planner mentioned.

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from cost, give ONE practical reason the planner may still choose the MORE EXPENSIVE company. Write a full sentence.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Practical, valid reason ✓
Mark 2: Written as a full sentence ✓

Accept any ONE valid reason, e.g.
• "Five large buses are easier to coordinate and arrive together compared with nine separate minibuses."
• "Large buses keep all the guests together, which is more comfortable for elderly guests and easier for the photographer to gather everyone."
• "Fewer vehicles means less risk of one minibus getting lost or running late."
• "Larger buses may have luggage space, air-conditioning, or be more comfortable for the guests."

subQuestions.questionText: Make a final recommendation to the wedding planner. State which company you would choose and JUSTIFY your decision using BOTH the cost calculation AND a real-life reason.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: A clear recommendation (Company X or Company Y) with cost reference ✓
Mark 2: A real-life reason that supports the chosen company ✓

Either choice is acceptable, provided the candidate uses BOTH the cost AND a real-life reason.

Example 1 (Company Y): "I would recommend COMPANY Y because it saves the wedding $R2\,950,00$, which can be used elsewhere on the wedding (cost reason). Although there are 9 minibuses, the planner can put one wedding co-ordinator in each minibus to keep them together."

Example 2 (Company X): "I would recommend COMPANY X — although it costs $R2\,950,00$ more, having only 5 buses keeps the 124 guests together and arriving at the same time, which is important for the wedding ceremony schedule."
